subject: EdgeCommerce: sudden P95/P99 spikes after A/B model swap
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@edgecommerce.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: [EdgeCommerce] Sharp P95/P99 latency increase after A/B swap

Hi Nikhil / Monica,

We just noticed a sharp degradation in latency on our production calls to Redwood hosted API starting at ~08:50 PDT. We were in the middle of an A/B experiment (routing ~30% to the new model variant v4). After the swap began the P95 jumped from ~650ms to ~2.1s and P99 shot up to ~4s; a few requests timed out and our frontend surfaced user-facing errors. Error rate on request throughput increased from ~0.2% to ~1.7% over the 25 minute window.

Attached is a CSV with sample p95/p99 snapshots and a text file showing representative request payloads. Can you confirm whether something changed on your side (model swap, config, or rollout policy)? This is affecting checkout flows; we need an urgent mitigation and timeline.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeCommerce

Attachment: request_snippets_20270412.txt (TXT)

We're pulling the telemetry now to correlate host-side metrics. Initial quick checks don't show a platform-wide incident, which points to something path- or model-specific for your routing. I’ve looped Marissa and our reliability lead Ben.

Immediate next steps:
- I will ask our reliability team to prioritize an investigation (Ben).
- Please confirm whether you have any recent client-side changes (headers, model tags, batching).
- We can temporarily pin your traffic to the previous variant (v3) while we triage — would you like us to do that now?

I’ll update in 20 minutes with telemetry. Apologies for the disruption.

— Nikhil

Folks — forwarding an active customer escalation (EdgeCommerce). Key facts:
- Started ~08:50 PDT; customer A/B routing: A = v3, B = v4 (~30% traffic)
- Customer-observed metrics: P95 from ~650ms -> ~2.1s, P99 ~4s; error rate +1.5pp
- Affected flow: checkout/price preview calls (latency-sensitive)

Can you investigate whether this is a model-variant regression (v4) or a routing/queueing change? Priority: either 1) mitigate customer (pin to v3 / rollback variant for customer), or 2) implement a fallback rule for your routing policy.

Relevant links: JIRA PERF-4521, telemetry folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDEfG-edge-telemetry
Attaching the request snippets they provided.

Thanks — we should aim for a DM in 15 mins with an action.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: [EdgeCommerce] Sharp P95/P99 latency increase after A/B swap — urgent

Quick update from reliability triage:
- Observed increased KV cache miss rate for variant v4 (approx +12% miss delta vs v3) which correlates with larger backend work on the GPU path.
- Queueing on the serving frontend for v4 pods increased median queue length by ~3x during the spike window.
- We also see occasional kernel fallbacks on the quantized execution path for v4 models (increasing tail latency).

Immediate mitigations we can do in the next 10-25 minutes:
1) Pin EdgeCommerce routing for production to variant v3 (rollback for that customer only) — this is low risk and reversible.
2) If they prefer platform-side fix first, we can throttle new v4 canary rollouts and add a route-level circuit breaker.

I recommend option (1) to stop user impact immediately. I’ll prepare the rollback runbook and execute once we have authorization.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Reliability — Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — thank you for the quick signal and the artifacts. Wanted to share what we’re going to do immediately to stop user impact:

1) We will pin your production traffic back to variant v3 within the next 15 minutes. This change is scoped to your account only and will not affect other customers.
2) Our reliability team (Ben) will continue root-cause analysis; we will provide a postmortem and timeline for a safe re-roll.
3) We will issue a 10% service credit for the affected window as a gesture — details and credits will be confirmed by Monica.

Proposed short call at 10:30 PDT to walk through the rollback and the data once we have telemetry. Let me know if that works.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
